messages:
morgan (DevEx): Quick help — our example-app tests started failing after the SDK moved to ESM-first. On GH Actions macOS/node16 we get "Unexpected token 'export'" when jest requires node_modules/@redwood/inference-js/dist/index.mjs. Locally on node18 it's fine. Any minimal fixes?

ravi (SDK): Did you publish both exports (import/require) in package.json? We intend to, but maybe the runner is resolving the .mjs straight. Can you paste jest config + package.json from the example app?

morgan (DevEx): jest.config.cjs is pretty standard: `preset: 'ts-jest', transformIgnorePatterns: ['/node_modules/']`. package.json of node_modules shows "exports": {"import": "./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"}.

jamie (Eng): Jest running under node16 will often try to require() and may see .mjs shim in resolution order for some reason (different resolver heuristics on runners). Two pragmatic approaches:
1) Whitelist the package in transformIgnorePatterns so Jest will transpile it. Example: `transformIgnorePatterns: ['/node_modules/(?!(?:@redwood/inference-js)/)']` and add an mjs transformer (esbuild-jest/@swc/jest).
2) Ship a tiny index.cjs at package root that `module.exports = require('./dist/index.cjs')` so require() path is plain CJS. This avoids having to transform node_modules in CI.

olga (QA): Also for tests that simulate edge runtime we hit missing webcrypto and fetch. Polyfill in setup files works: create `test/setupPolyfills.js` and add `setupFilesAfterEnv`/`setupFiles` pointing to it. For node16: `const { webcrypto } = require('node:crypto'); global.crypto = webcrypto; global.fetch = require('node-fetch')` (or undici).

morgan (DevEx): I tried whitelisting but then ts-jest + swc mismatched TS emitting and some modules failed with "Cannot use import statement outside a module". The CJS shim approach seems simpler. Ravi, can SDK publish that?

ravi (SDK): Yes — I'll publish a patch that adds `index.cjs` root shim and also adds `export { default } from './dist/index.mjs'` in a small index.mjs re-export so both patterns work. In the meantime, you can add a test-only shim: in jest `setupFiles` do `const sdk = require('@redwood/inference-js'); if (sdk && !sdk.default) sdk.default = sdk.createClient || (() => {});` — ugly but stabilizes CI.

jamie (Eng): And add a small manual mock for auth flows instead of requiring the package to be transformed. Jest manual mock at `__mocks__/@redwood/inference-js.js` exporting the functions your tests expect will be used automatically. That avoids messing with module resolution.

olga (QA): Once the SDK patch is published I'll run the mac/node16 CI job multiple times to confirm flakes are gone. Also adding a smoke test in SDK repo that runs `node -e "console.log(require('@redwood/inference-js'))"` under node16 helps catch resolver regressions.

morgan (DevEx): Perfect. Filed RED-4712 with repro steps + CI logs and linked to the SDK PR. Thanks everyone. If anyone else hits ESM/CJS test flakiness ping this thread and paste stack + jest/vitest config. :pray:
